chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Abdillah al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, the Quraysh in the pre-Islamic period demolished the House. When they intended to build it, there was an impediment placed between them and it, and awe was instilled in their hearts, until a speaker from among them said: Let each man bring the best of his wealth, and do not bring any wealth that you have earned through cutting off family ties or forbidden means. So they did so, and the way was cleared between them and building it.

So they built it until they reached the place of the Black Stone. They quarrelled about which of them would place the Black Stone in its position, to the extent that evil nearly broke out among them. They agreed that the first one to enter through the gate of the Masjid would decide. Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) entered.

When he came to them, he ordered a cloth to be spread out, then placed the Stone in the middle of it. Then the tribes grasped the sides of the cloth and raised it. Then he (peace be upon him and his family) took it and placed it in its position. Thus God distinguished him for it.

key_terms.البيت: The House — the Kaaba in Mecca, the cubic structure at the centre of the Grand Mosque, considered the most sacred site in Islam
key_terms.الجاهلية: The pre-Islamic period of ignorance (Jahiliyya) — the era before the advent of Islam, characterised by tribal feuds, polytheism, and moral disorder
key_terms.الحجر الأسود: The Black Stone (al-Hajar al-Aswad) — a stone embedded in the eastern corner of the Kaaba, believed to have descended from paradise
key_terms.فخصه الله به: God distinguished/honoured him for it — indicating divine selection of the Prophet for this honour even before his formal prophethood
key_terms.قطيعة رحم: Cutting off of family ties (qati'at al-rahim) — severing kinship bonds, strongly condemned in Islamic ethics

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad resolve the dispute over placing the Black Stone in the Kaaba?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates this important historical account of how the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) wisely resolved a potentially violent tribal dispute over who should place the Black Stone during the Quraysh's reconstruction of the Kaaba before his prophethood. The incident took place during the Quraysh's rebuilding effort in the pre-Islamic period (Jahiliyya), when they had demolished and were reconstructing the Kaaba. The Prophet's divinely-guided arbitration — using a garment so that all tribes could simultaneously participate in lifting the Stone to its position — averted a civil war among the Arabian tribes and demonstrated his unique status before God.
